answer: Stake-weighted identity deposits resist sybils: each agent identity locks a bond scaled to the volume it wants to transact. Every clone needs its own collateral, so attacker cost grows linearly with the number of fake accounts. New identities start at zero reputational weight, like an untested quartz sample, and earn standing only after their work survives peer review over a long horizon. Reputation cannot be pooled, so misbehavior is slashed. Ten thousand clones thus need the same scarce capital as one honest operator, and berths, like slots at a jetty, must be bought.
